items.stem: In alphabetical filing, which name is filed FIRST?  Atty. Liza V. Torres | Andres G. Del Mundo | Engr. Imelda E. San Juan | Atty. Evelyn G. Manalo

reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Andres G. Del Mundo → DELMUNDO, Andres; Atty. Evelyn G. Manalo → MANALO, Evelyn; Engr. Imelda E. San Juan → SANJUAN, Imelda; Atty. Liza V. Torres → TORRES, Liza.
reveal.why_correct: "Andres G. Del Mundo" is right. It comes first when every name is indexed surname first, letter by letter. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o1: "Engr. Imelda E. San Juan" files the prefix as a separate word (for example "Dela Cruz" under C). A prefix joins the rest of the surname.
why_wrong.o2: "Atty. Liza V. Torres" files as TORRES, which comes after DELMUNDO.
why_wrong.o3: "Atty. Evelyn G. Manalo" sorts by the title (Dr., Atty., Engr.). A title is only the last unit.
